newsitem.title: UK: Nickel at the lowest in 2-1/4 years.
newsitem.headline: Nickel at the lowest in 2-1/4 years.

text.p: The price of nickel fell to its lowest in 2-1/4 years on the London Metal Exchange on Monday as a less robust global economic expansion caught up with it. Traders said hitherto strong demand for stainless steel, which accounts for 60 percent of nickel consumption, had slackened and consumers were drawing on their stocks. A late sell-off took the market down to its low of $6,365 per tonne, down $111 from Friday. Other industrial metals were quiet, as were most commodities, ahead of the New Year holiday. Gold closed in London little changed at $369.10/$369.60 which was down 20 cents from Friday. But silver ended 10 cents lower at $4.80/$4.82 an ounce following a New York-led sell off. And winter chills sent oil prices surging again as European buyers rushed to cover seasonal demand.
London February futures for bellwether North Sea Brent Blend crude oil jumped 44 cents to $23.86 a barrel before easing slightly later in the day.

"I'm sure that gas oil (heating oil) has fuelled the move higher today with the severe winter weather we're seeing across the continent," said analyst Tim Holmes at brokerage Mees Pierson Derivatives. London white sugar futures edged up in volume which traders described as good considering that many market players were absent ahead of the New Year holiday.

Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) benchmark March wheat futures eased. Icy and rainy weather in the Pacific Northwest has virtually stoppped all transportation, so the pace of North American wheat exports was seen slackening, traders said. Some key Commodity prices at 1700 GMT on Monday
